campaign.title: Derive and test the combined M1/M2 top-cone architecture

conductor_policy.monitoring: Check all constants, characters, Vaaler variables, cone boundaries, endpoint terms, and whether any purported M1/M2 cancellation preserves the actual profiles.
conductor_policy.round_close: Close with an exact combined formula and either a target estimate, a strictly smaller signed kernel, or a rigorous no-go showing the cones do not cancel.

numerical_purpose: falsify an exact coefficient, cone, or pairing identity
resource_policy.numerical_prohibition: Numerical agreement cannot promote an asymptotic estimate.
resource_policy.literature_policy: Use primary sources only if importing a transformation or bilinear theorem.

frozen_target.M2_cone: The accepted top M2 cone has h odd, ceil(h/4)<=m<=h, phase e(sqrt(Xhm)), and character chi_4(h).
frozen_target.combined_question: Derive the top M1 transform with the same conventions and decide exactly whether its stationary cone is complementary to the M2 cone after relabeling, and whether constants/profiles cancel, reinforce, or leave a smaller boundary kernel.
frozen_target.success: Prove an O_epsilon(X^(1/4+epsilon)) bound for the combined top sawtooth contribution and separately identify what is still needed for M1/M2 blockwise obligations, or rigorously rule out the combined-cone mechanism.

exit_gates: exact M1 one-sided transform with actual chi_4(d)
M1 boundary and error sizes after actual alpha weights
exact M1/M2 cone comparison and constants
campaign.promotion_policy: Do not replace the proof architecture by a combined bound unless its implication to the original balanced sawtooth formula is exact. A combined cancellation does not by itself prove the separately stated M9 obligation; record the weakest correct bridge.
